title: Lentil and Bacon Soup
subtitle: Chunky red lentil soup with smoked bacon and vegetables
excerpt: Smoked bacon lardons fried until crisp, then simmered with red lentils, carrots, and onion until the lentils collapse into a thick, warming broth. A one-pot supper that keeps and reheats well.

recipe.sourceNotes: Red lentils are one of the most practical ingredients for home cooking: they need no soaking, cook in 20 minutes, and dissolve naturally into stock to create a thick soup without any blending. Smoked bacon adds depth and a savoury backbone. The soup thickens considerably as it stands; add a splash of water when reheating.

content.text: Red lentils dissolve completely as they cook: no blending is needed. Fry the bacon first so the fat renders into the pot and flavours the vegetables. The soup is ready when the lentils have completely broken down and there is no visible whole lentil remaining.

Fry the lardons in a large saucepan over medium heat for 5 minutes until beginning to colour. Add the onion, carrot, and celery. Cook for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed red lentils, tinned tomatoes, bay leaf, and hot stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils have completely dissolved and the soup is thick.
Remove the bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper. Taste: the soup should be well seasoned and deeply savoury from the bacon and lentils combined. Serve with crusty bread.
